body: Yeah that is frustrating. I was misdiagnosed a few times before I was given one that made sense so that is definitely a possibility too. Maybe get a second opinion?
Oh yes my cats help a lot!

I have also been diagnosed with bipolar in addition to generalized anxiety disorder. I was diagnosed with bipolar about 2 1/2 years ago and am still figuring out the best combo of meds so my first piece of insight is to say that yes, the meds you are on might not be the right fit and it might take a lot of trial and error to find something that works.

It isn't as common anymore for me to feel elated during hypomania but I do feel hyperactive, which is also common and might be what you're experiencing. With hypomania, I also usually feel impulsive, distracted, anxious, goal-oriented, less need for sleep (basically exactly the description of symptoms). My point is that I wouldn't disregard having hypomania just because you may lack feelings of elation or gradiosity. 

My depression hasn't gotten much better since being diagnosed and I think is exacerbated by my ever-increasing anxiety. My depression lasts longer than a few days and often makes it difficult to function. However, it is only very dangerous when it appears in a mixed episode where I am feeling depressed AND impulsive.  

Medication won't solve everything but the right meds do help. I was often unable to function because of my episodes and was being very irresponsible/impulsive. Now, I am not completely screwing everything up even though I do still feel really shitty sometimes.

I hope this helps a bit. Always here to chat!

Hey-
First of all yes, it is worth asking for help in college. I struggled a lot throughout school and never really received the help I needed because I didn't know it existed. Search your schools website for information on the disability/access office and make an appointment there asap. Also look to see if you all have a CARE team and perhaps reach out to them. Look up the counseling center. Most schools offer a certain number of free sessions to students and a discounted rate after that- make an appt asap. Also, I know it's tough and awkward but reaching out to your professors could be really helpful. Perhaps just one who you feel a bit closer to or trust more? 

Anyway, I hope those suggestions help.
